1.explanation:
• BpmnConnectSnapping.js and BpmnSnappingUtil.js handle where connectors (including message flows) may attach to element boundaries. A stale lane-header boundary ends up in their hit-testing logic after a split+remove.  
• CreateParticipantBehavior.js, RemoveParticipantBehavior.js and ResizeLaneBehavior.js govern creation, deletion and resizing of pools and lanes; an out-of-sync geometry after remove distorts the target shape’s boundaries.  
• LaneUtil.js maintains the pool↔lane containment model and the header vs body region; if it doesn’t correctly recalculate the pool’s interior when a lane is removed, snapping code will only see the header.  
• LineAttachmentUtil.js and LineIntersect.js compute the exact docking point on a shape’s perimeter for a connector; with an incorrect perimeter after lane-removal, these routines will exclude the body edge and force attachment at the header.  
Together, these files determine how pool boundaries are exposed to the connection tool. Fixing the lane-removal geometry update and the snapping intersection logic in them will restore the original behavior where you can click anywhere on the pool body to attach a message flow.
1.bug_scenario: When connecting two pools with a message flow, you normally click inside the body of one pool and then inside the body of the other. If you add a lane to a pool and immediately remove it, however, that target pool’s body no longer accepts the message flow drop at the inner lane boundary — you can only drop at the top header section. The GIF shows how, after split-and-remove, the connector refuses to snap to the pool’s body and instead jumps up into the header area.

2.explanation:
• DeleteLaneBehavior.js  
  This behavior runs when you remove a lane. It is responsible for reshaping the participant when lanes are removed. It currently leaves the participant in a state where only its header region is considered a valid connection target. We need to adjust it so that after you delete back to one lane, the remaining lane shape is promoted to act as the full body again.  

• LaneUtil.js  
  This utility computes lane bounds and the division between header vs. body in a pool. When there’s only one lane left, it should treat that single lane as the full participant region — not just a nested child. The hit-box math here must be updated so that a single-lane pool expends to its full bounds.  

• BpmnRules.js  
  The canConnect/connect rules for message flows identify participants (pools) and lanes, and currently only allow attaching at the participant header, not at a lone lane. We must extend the rule to also accept a single remaining lane as a valid message flow target.  

• BpmnConnectSnapping.js  
  This module defines where connector endpoints snap to shapes (e.g. on header, on body). It still calculates snap-zones based on the old pool/lane hierarchy, so when you revert to one lane it only offers the header snap box. Updating its zone computation will let you grab the side of the single lane again.
2.bug_scenario: When a pool (participant) once had more than one lane, and you delete back down to a single lane, the diagram no longer lets you attach a message flow to the body of the pool (i.e. the remaining lane shape) — you can only target the header area of the participant. Before ever adding/removing a lane you could freely create message flows by clicking on either pool’s body. After adding then removing a lane, the pool’s hit-area for message-flow attachment collapses to just the header region.
